cells.tense: You are the one who is gone into what a feeling is while it is still here.
cells.ask: At one gathering this week, tell the story behind one thing you all do, not just the practice. What the telling gives back is yours to keep.
cells.core:
Whatever you're feeling, you're in it — all the way, while it's still happening. Not deciding whether it belongs or what it's for. You let the song, the food, the light at that table sit in you until they've gone quiet on their own.

That depth is why people bring their hard news to you. They feel you receiving it, and not taking it over. There's more under this than showing up the same way each time. When you've really sat with something and know its shape, hand one piece into the line you're part of — one story, one practice. Someone else can carry it too, and that's what keeps it alive.
cells.sheetLine: You feel it all the way down, while it's still here.
cells.verb: Be gone into what a feeling is while it is still here
cells.place: The table where the old songs get sung and the same stories get told

cells.tense: You will be coiling against how the next quieter season will feel before it has started.
cells.ask: Say one true hard thing about the last change out loud, then leave the ending alone for a week. What you've gathered is yours to keep either way.
cells.core:
You're already bracing for the quiet after the gathering — for a time when the table won't feel the same, before anything has actually changed. So you hold onto the feeling, replay it, try to keep the good part from moving at all.

It doesn't work. Holding on that hard turns the warmth into a countdown, and you end up grieving a loss that hasn't landed. Good gatherings end. That's not a failure of the gathering — it's what makes them worth having had. Let the last one close, and the next one will have somewhere to arrive. What you're calling care for them right now is keeping you out of the room.

cells.tense: You sat with what you felt while it was still warm, and you have not returned to that sitting.
cells.ask: Name one thing you felt at the last gathering, plainly, to one person who was there. Just saying it — nothing else has to follow.
cells.core:
You're at the table, and a song comes up, and you reach for your phone. The warmth is there; you're just not going in with it. This is how it runs now, and it costs you the middle of the evening.

It's not that you don't feel. You ask about someone's week, you do your part, and none of it arrives in you while it's happening. That's a numbness you built on purpose. Start smaller than you think. One word for one thing you felt, said to someone who was in the room, puts the current back where it belongs — after the fact, which is still fine.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped going into what you felt, and you're still carrying the habit.

cells.tense: Reverie is at work in how you stand in the shared history, without your knowing you are the one holding it.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing people bring you their hard news for is your doing. Watch what shifts this week when you keep it.
cells.core:
Something in the way you are with feeling is already shaping the common life around you — the long pauses, the lost look before you answer — and you treat it like it happens to you. But you're the one who stands in it long enough to find the questions that hold people together.

That's yours. Not the song, not the table — you. Stand five seconds longer in the pause and then ask the one question that opens things. The stillness you call your nature is the line running the room; the pen is in your hand whether or not you've said so.
cells.sheetLine: The room's depth is your doing, and you haven't said so.
